---
name: ptk-shared-configs
description: Synchronize pinned external configuration bases, author pre-commit or clang overlays, diagnose hash drift, export deviation reports or set up local Git hooks in a PTk project. Preserve project-owned Ruff settings and maintainer-only synchronization.
---

# ptk-shared-configs

First follow the [project discovery and execution guide](../../../docs/guides/agent-guide.rst). Apply it even when this skill is invoked directly; examples are syntax references, not project defaults.

1. Read [external configuration ownership](../../../docs/guides/shared-configs.rst) and inspect the runtime schema with `ptk describe --json --configuration` (or the bundled schema when runtime inspection is unavailable).
2. Declare a general `source.repository` and `source.revision` plus per-group `files` mappings with `source` and `destination`. PTk ships no bases. Use an explicit version tag (up to four numeric parts, e.g. `v2.4.0` or `v26.45.00.01`) or full commit hash, never an invented repository or floating branch. A `source` and `destination` both ending in `/` copy a folder recursively; both sides must be folders and folder mappings cannot have an overlay.
3. External destinations are unchanged copies. Never edit them in the consuming project. Inspect their provenance, content hashes and originating `mapping` in `.ptk-configs.lock.json` inside the project’s `repository.config_path` directory. Files removed upstream from a mapped folder stay until deleted.
4. For pre-commit/clang customization, author a project-owned `overlay` and a separate generated `output`. Never merge into the base. Preserve native merge semantics. Outputs start with a `# Generated by PTK; do not edit...` header; edit the overlay instead.
5. For Ruff, author project-owned `ruff.toml` with native `extend` pointing to the external copy. Ruff has no overlay/generation mode.
6. Use `ptk maintainer sync configs [NAMES] [--check|--diff]` (`--check` and `--diff` are mutually exclusive; NAMES must be enabled groups). Preview with `--diff`, apply without options, then run offline `ptk validate --generated` (maintainers can also use `--check`). There is no configs.sync step; jobs must not synchronize policy.
7. Commit the source mapping, bases, lock, overlays and generated results together. Change revision explicitly to upgrade; a locked tag does not follow tag movement. After a source/revision change, synchronize all groups together (naming groups is rejected). Resolve modified-file conflicts through review, never force overwrite.
8. Files remain writable. Offline checks compare contents/executable bits; use `ptk maintainer configs-report` to export effective deviations and modified base filenames. The lock is provenance, not independent authentication.
9. Report deviations from current generated YAML, not a hypothetical newly merged overlay. Modified bases are listed separately and never used as diff references; missing files remain unavailable. Project-owned Ruff inheritance is outside comparison scope. The report is not a freshness gate: use `ptk validate --generated` for that.

10. Removing mappings leaves files untouched. Review obsolete files and run affected linters/formatters. Commit or push only within authorized scope.

11. With `configs.pre-commit.enabled: true`, commit the final project-owned or generated pre-commit configuration
    (`.pre-commit-config.yaml` unless `hook_config` selects another path)
    before developers run jobs. Local jobs automatically install/repair the hooks;
    workflows check each participating repository before starting jobs. This works
    for normal users and does not synchronize configuration. Help, previews, CX,
    and disabled entries do not install hooks. Diagnose with `ptk self-service doctor`.

12. Preserve existing hooks and custom Git settings. Resolve `core.hooksPath`,
    hook-file symlink or `.legacy` backup conflicts with the maintainer; do not
    blindly remove them. Use the same relative config path across linked worktrees.
    Local installation happens before real jobs, not at clone or extension activation. For onboarding before a first commit, use `ptk self-service hooks install`; inspect with `hooks status`. Do not expand a local setup request into CX changes.

`maintainer sync configs` (including `--diff`) requires a login ID
listed in the configuration folder's `maintainers.ptk.yml`. `validate --generated`
checks generated configuration without writing and is available to normal users. Verify identity with `self-service doctor`; do not suggest
`PTK_ROLE=maintainer` as a workaround. See the maintainer section of the
[configuration guide](../../../docs/guides/configuration.rst).
